characterization_methods.key_findings: The Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni alloy shows a two-phase microstructure: a grey γ matrix with bright white B2 particles decorating grain boundaries and grain interiors (Fig. 1c).
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe the microstructure of the as-cast plus homogenised alloy

characterization_methods.key_findings: Analysed composition of the 28Mn5Ni homogenised ingot (wt%): Mn 28.1, Al 8.6, C 0.9, Ni 4.8, Fe balance.
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine the chemical composition of the homogenised ingots
characterization_methods.technique: Wet chemical analysis / standard emission spectroscopy

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting (VIM) of the alloy into a 30 kg ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Three austenitic LDS grades including 28Mn5Ni were prepared by the vacuum induction melting route; the defect-free portions of the 30 kg as-cast ingots were used further.
Defect-free portions of the 30 kg as-cast ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours; this as-cast plus homogenised condition is the precursor/starting condition prior to hot rolling.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grey matrix grains forming the continuous phase
bright white second-phase particles decorating grain boundaries and located inside the grey γ grains

structures.overall_structure: In the as-cast plus homogenised condition the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni alloy (Fe-28Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C) consists of two phases: a grey γ (austenite) matrix with bright white B2 second-phase particles decorating the grain boundaries and the grain interiors.

unmapped_findings: Analysed chemical composition of the homogenised 28Mn5Ni (Fe-28Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C) ingot (Table 1, wt%): Mn 28.1, Al 8.6, C 0.9, Ni 4.8, Fe balance.
The as-cast plus homogenised condition of 28Mn5Ni is the precursor/starting condition prior to hot rolling of the homogenised ingots at 1323 K (total ~85% thickness reduction with ~15% per pass).

No mechanical (hardness or tensile) property data, no XRD phase-fraction values and no TEM/ACOM deformation data are reported in the paper for the as-cast plus homogenised condition of 28Mn5Ni; the reported hardness (HV256/268/375), nanoindentation, tensile (YS/UTS/elongation) and deformation-microstructure data all pertain to the hot-rolled condition of the alloys (different process) and are therefore excluded from this as-homogenised sample.
